properties.answer: Anthony, 2026-07-28: "go ahead with req:seam-incompatibility". BUILT as `seam_report`. Compares paired boundaries across eight axes — medium, paradigm, payload_format, auth, transport_security, operations, error_model, payload_schema — and classifies each as agreed / incompatible / differs / unstated. Three rules, all from what the trial established: `unspecified` on either side is UNSTATED and never agreement, so "0 incompatibilities" can never be read as compatible; free-text axes report as DIFFERS for a person, never as incompatible, because a machine cannot tell a real mismatch from different wording; and the report always names what it did NOT examine (con:pairing-stops-at-the-boundary — the types that CROSS a boundary are invisible to it). Pairing is supplied rather than computed, because the subscribe side is not declarable until req:complementary-pairing lands.

properties.question: reflow2 can tell you when a connection between two projects is missing a side, but not when both sides exist and simply disagree — one sending a format the other does not expect, or one assuming a speed the other cannot meet. That is the failure that survives testing until it does not. Do you want reflow2 to catch that, knowing it only works once the connection details above are captured properly?
